chunks: Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said:
“Two bloods in Islam are permissible from Allah, Blessed and Exalted; no one shall judge concerning them until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends forth our Qāʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt.
Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends forth our Qāʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt, he will judge regarding them by the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
The muḥṣan adulterer—he will stone him; and the withholder of zakat—he will strike his neck.”

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The Household of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الزَّانِي الْمُحْصَنُ: The married adulterer subject to rajm
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: The religion within whose legal order these rulings are mentioned
key_terms.قَائِمَنَا: Our Qāʾim, the one who will arise from the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: Which punishments does this hadith say will be carried out by the Qāʾim of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith states that two specific cases involving lawful bloodshed in Islam are deferred until the rise of the Qāʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt. It identifies these as the punishment of the muḥṣan adulterer and the execution of the one who withholds zakat, emphasizing the authority of the divinely guided ruler in implementing Allah’s judgment.
